sourcedFrom: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series (Published August 26, 2024)
cleanIntro: A 2011 strip straight out of Staccato's own CS instructions: slide stop lever down, slide stop out, slide forward off the frame, then the Dawson Precision Light Recoil System drawn forward by its flange, down off the barrel and out the back of the spring tunnel, and the barrel out the front. Staccato states the procedure is the same for the 2023 and 2024 CS. ⛔ This is not the strip for the Staccato C, C2, P, XC or XL — each has its own recoil step.

steps.title: Muzzle in a safe direction
steps.action: Start with the pistol pointed somewhere safe and keep it that way through the whole strip. Staccato opens the CS procedure with this before anything else is touched, because the next step works the slide.
steps.quote: Ensure the pistol is pointed in a safe direction.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 1

steps.title: Racked, then chamber and magazine well both checked
steps.action: Rack the slide to the rear and look into the chamber and into the magazine well — both places, not one. An empty chamber over a loaded magazine is still a loaded pistol the moment the slide goes forward again.
steps.quote: Rack the slide to the rear and visually inspect the chamber and magazine well make sure the pistol is empty.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 2

steps.title: Takedown notch lined up with the slide stop knuckle
steps.action: The slide stop is what holds the top end on the lower, so it comes out first. Draw the slide back until the takedown notch sits over the knuckle of the slide stop and hold it there. If the notch is off the knuckle, the slide stop will not come out cleanly.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back to line up to take down notch on the slide with the slide stop knuckle.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, steps 3–4

steps.title: Slide stop lever pushed all the way down against the frame
steps.action: With the notch held on the knuckle, push down on the slide stop lever until it sits all the way down against the frame. Staccato puts this before the pin is touched on the CS — a lever left part-way up is what makes the slide stop bind on the way out.
steps.quote: Push down on the slide stop lever to ensure it's lowered all the way down against your frame.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 5

steps.title: Slide stop pin pushed from the opposite side, slide stop out
steps.action: Push the slide stop pin from the far side of the pistol with a finger or a small tool, then take the slide stop out. It should move under light pressure; if it resists, the notch has drifted off the knuckle or the lever is not fully down.
steps.quote: And then push on the slide stop pin from the opposite side of the pistol using your finger or a small tool, and then move the slide stop.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 5

steps.title: Slide eased forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide gently forward and off the frame rails. Gently is Staccato's word — the slide carries the barrel and the recoil system with it, and nothing on this step needs force.
steps.quote: Gently pull the slide forward and off of the frame.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 6

steps.title: Light Recoil System forward by its flange, down off the barrel, out the back
steps.action: Take the Dawson Precision Light Recoil System by its flange, pull it forward slightly and down off the barrel, then draw it out the back of the spring tunnel. This is the CS's own recoil step — it comes out the back, not the front and not the shooter side.
steps.quote: Remove the Dawson Precision® Light Recoil System by pulling the flange forward slightly and down off of the barrel. Pull it out the back of the spring tunnel.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 7

steps.title: Link forward, barrel out of the muzzle end
steps.action: Slide the link forward along the barrel, then draw the barrel out of the muzzle end of the slide. That completes the strip — frame, slide stop, slide, recoil system and barrel. Staccato publishes nothing further than this for the CS.
steps.quote: Slide the link forward on the barrel and pull the barrel out of the muzzle end of the slide.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 8

steps.title: Rails, frame surfaces and feed ramp brushed and wiped
steps.action: With your brush attachments and a rag or paper towel, clear the debris off the slide rails, the frame surfaces and the feed ramp.
steps.prose: The feed ramp is the one most often skipped. Carbon there is where feeding trouble starts, and the rails carry the grit the slide rides on every shot.
steps.quote: Use your brush attachments and a cleaning rag or paper towel to clear away debris from the slide rails and the frame surfaces and feed ramp.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: Bore brushed breech to muzzle on the memory flex cable
steps.action: Run the bore brush through the barrel on the memory flex cable, from the breech to the muzzle, as many times as it takes.
steps.prose: Breech to muzzle pushes the fouling out the front instead of back into the chamber.
steps.quote: Use your bore brush to clean the bore of your barrel, utilizing the memory flex cable to brush the bore from the breech to the muzzle. Repeat this step as needed.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: Bore oiled with the mop, excess wiped back out
steps.action: Put a small amount of CLP on the bore mop and oil the bore, then wipe the excess oil out of the inside of the barrel with a clean patch.
steps.prose: The clean patch at the end is the point — a film of oil in the bore, not a wet one.
steps.quote: Apply a small amount of CLP to your bore mop and oil the bore of your barrel.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: A few drops on the slide rails and barrel contact points
steps.action: Put a few drops of lubricant on the slide rails and on the barrel's contact points, and no more.
steps.prose: Staccato says a few drops. More than that does not make the pistol run better — it holds powder residue and grit where the slide and barrel move.
steps.quote: Apply a few drops of lubricant to your slide rails and barrel contact points.
steps.cite: Staccato CS Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

deepAbsentReason: Staccato publishes this page as basic disassembly and reassembly — the article describes itself as covering 'basic disassembly/reassembly of the Staccato CS', and it ends at frame, slide stop, slide, recoil system and barrel. No extractor, firing pin, sear, mainspring housing or grip-module procedure is published on it, and no exploded view accompanies it. For anything further, the page directs owners to contact Staccato Customer Service directly. Nothing deeper was invented from it.

cleaning.name: RAILS, FRAME & FEED RAMP
tasks: Brush and wipe debris off the slide rails
Brush and wipe the frame surfaces

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush the bore from breech to muzzle using the memory flex cable, repeating as needed
Put a small amount of CLP on a bore mop and oil the bore
Wipe the excess oil out of the barrel with a clean patch

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A few drops of lubricant on the slide rails
A few drops on the barrel contact points

reassembly: Check the link is flipped forward toward the muzzle, then reinstall the barrel.
Insert the recoil system into the spring tunnel of the slide and align it against the barrel lugs.

Line the slide rails up with the frame rails and run the slide on. Staccato's own note: the guide rod flange must be pushed up all the way against the barrel and not kicking out toward the frame, and the barrel must not be rotated to either side, or the top end will not slide fully onto the lower.

Look through the slide stop hole in the frame for the link — the pin on the slide stop must pass through the hole in the link or the pistol will not function. If it is not lined up, drop it into place with a small tool.
Insert the slide stop into the frame through the link hole and rest it gently against the frame.
Pull the slide back to line the takedown notch up with the knuckle on the slide stop, then seat the slide stop fully into the frame.
Rack the slide to check for proper function.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, rack the slide several times and confirm it returns fully into battery, then check the slide stop is fully seated in the frame — a slide stop that will not seat has missed the hole in the barrel link.
